title: The Bosphorus Brief — 26 August 2026
overview: The big legal story today is the European Court of Human Rights' Grand Chamber ruling on Osman Kavala, ordering his immediate release. Regionally, the Strait of Hormuz situation appears to be easing, and Turkey's central bank is resuming a key monetary tool. Locally, expect minor seismic activity to continue and lira rates to hold fairly steady.
sections: <parameter name="body">The ECtHR Grand Chamber issued a second, firmer ruling on Osman Kavala's case, convicting Turkey on five counts and declaring his original conviction "null and void." The court has ordered his immediate release. Independent outlets (Medyascope, Bianet, T24) and international coverage (Euronews, BBC, DW) framed this as a significant legal rebuke, while Amnesty International and the Media and Law Studies Association called for swift compliance. No pro-government outlet coverage of the ruling appeared in today's material — a gap worth noting for residents tracking how this story is discussed across the media landscape. For foreign residents, this case is a bellwether for how Turkey's courts and government respond to binding international human rights rulings; there is no indication yet of Ankara's next move, and we'll follow this closely.
heading: ECtHR Orders Kavala's Release
